:::{#sol-full-column-rank-practice}

Yes.
Suppose $c_1 \tp{(1, 1, 1)} + c_2 \tp{(2, 4, 6)} = \vzero$.
The first two entries give

$$
c_1 + 2 c_2 = 0
\quad \text{and} \quad
c_1 + 4 c_2 = 0.
$$

Subtracting the first equation from the second gives $2 c_2 = 0$,
so $c_2 = 0$,
and then $c_1 = 0$.
So the two [columns of $\matr{X}$](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-column) are [linearly independent](#def-linearly-independent),
the [rank](#def-rank) of $\matr{X}$ is $2$,
and $\matr{X}$ has [full column rank](#def-full-column-rank).

:::
